q: When passing a cyclist, how much space must you leave, where practical?
a: At least 1 metre
e: Minimum 1 m. Better: change lanes to pass when you can.
s: When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.

q: A streetcar is stopped and passengers are getting on and off. How far behind its rear doors must you stop?
a: At least 2 metres
e: 2 m behind the rear doors, unless there's a special safety island or zone for passengers.
s: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on.

q: It is illegal to follow a fire vehicle that is answering an alarm closer than…
a: 150 metres
e: Stay at least 150 m behind a fire vehicle answering an alarm.
s: it is illegal to follow within 150 metres of a fire vehicle responding to an alarm

q: Most tractors and combines have a maximum speed of about…
a: 40 km/h
e: They often go even slower when towing. Watch for the orange slow-moving vehicle sign.
s: Most tractors and combines have a maximum speed of 40 km/h

q: An ambulance with flashing lights and siren is coming up behind you. What must you do?
a: Pull as close as practical to the right edge, clear of intersections, and stop
w: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Stop right where you are in your lane
e: Signal, move right, stop parallel to the road, and wait until it passes.
s: you are required to bring your vehicle as near as is practical to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway

q: You're in an intersection waiting to turn left when an emergency vehicle comes with its siren on. What should you do?
a: Don't turn: go straight through when it's safe, then pull to the right and stop
w: Back up out of the intersection
e: Clearing the intersection straight ahead avoids a crash if the emergency vehicle passes on the side you meant to turn to.
s: you should abandon the turn and clear the intersection by proceeding straight when safe to do so, then pull to the right and stop

q: A car behind you has a flashing GREEN light on its dashboard. Who is it, and what should you do?
a: A volunteer firefighter or medical responder: yield to let them through
w: A police officer: pull over and wait for a ticket
e: Some firefighters and volunteer medical responders use a flashing green light in their own vehicles.
s: Some firefighters and volunteer medical responders may display a flashing green light when using their own vehicles to respond to a fire or medical emergency.

q: A horse-drawn buggy is coming toward you on a two-lane road. What should you do?
a: Move to the far right of your lane and slow down
w: Honk to let the driver know you're there
Speed up to pass it quickly
e: Give horses lots of room. Startling them can make them swerve.
s: When approaching a horse-drawn vehicle travelling in the opposite direction, move to the far right of your lane.

q: You're turning left. Two cyclists are coming toward you from the other direction. What do you do?
a: Stop and wait for the oncoming bicycles to pass before turning
w: Turn before them; cars have priority
e: Bicycles are vehicles. Wait for oncoming bikes just like oncoming cars.
s: When turning left, you must stop and wait for oncoming bicycles to pass before turning.

q: A cyclist ahead of you is turning left at an intersection. You're turning left too. What should you do?
a: Stay behind the cyclist and turn when the way is clear
w: Pull up beside the cyclist and turn together
Pass the cyclist on the right
e: Don't pull up beside a bike, motorcycle or moped turning left. Wait behind it.
s: If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.

q: An oncoming motorcycle has its turn signal on. You want to turn left in front of it. What should you do?
a: Make sure it's actually turning before you go: the rider may have forgotten to switch the signal off
e: Many motorcycle turn signals don't shut off by themselves.
s: Make sure the motorcyclist is actually turning; he or she may have just forgotten to switch off the turn signal.

q: A large truck ahead of you is making a right turn and swings wide to the left. A gap opens on its right. What should you do?
a: Stay well back until the truck has completely cleared the lane
w: Move into the gap and pass on the right
Honk so the truck moves back
Pass it on the left quickly
e: If you move into that space, you can get squeezed between the trailer and the curb.
s: Stay well back until the truck has completely cleared the lane.

q: You're in a roundabout when an emergency vehicle comes up behind you. What should you do?
a: Leave at your intended exit, drive past the traffic island, then pull over
w: Stop right away inside the roundabout
e: If you haven't entered yet, pull over to the right and wait.
s: If you are in a roundabout when an emergency vehicle approaches, exit at your intended exit and proceed beyond the traffic island before pulling over.

q: A police car with flashing lights is stopped on the shoulder. Your side of the highway has two lanes, and you're in the right lane. What must you do?
a: Slow down and, if safe, move into the lane away from it
w: Speed up to get past quickly
e: Slow down AND move over. It's 3 demerit points if you don't.
s: When the roadway has two or more lanes of traffic in the same direction of your travel, you are required to move into a lane away from the emergency vehicle or tow truck, if safe to do so

q: A tow truck with its amber lights flashing is stopped on the shoulder ahead, on your side of the road. What must you do?
a: Slow down and pass with caution, and move over a lane if there is one and it's safe
w: Nothing; the move-over law is only for police
e: The slow-down-and-move-over law covers tow trucks with flashing amber lights too.
s: a tow truck with its amber lights flashing in the same direction of your travel, you are required to reduce the speed of your vehicle and proceed with caution

q: You're turning right into a driveway, across a bike lane marked with a solid white line. What should you do?
a: Enter the bike lane only after making sure it's safe, then turn
w: Turn quickly; bike lanes are optional
Honk to warn cyclists, then turn
Stop in the bike lane and wait
e: Bike lanes are for cyclists. Check for bikes before you cross into it.
s: Enter the bike lane only after ensuring that you can do so safely, and then make the turn.

q: A pedestrian with a white cane is waiting to cross at the corner where you're turning. What should you do?
a: Yield and give them time and space to cross
w: Honk so they know you're there
Drive past quickly before they start
Wave them across from your car
e: A white cane or guide dog means the person is blind or has low vision. In most cases, drivers yield to pedestrians.
s: Pedestrians who are blind or with a visual disability may use a white cane or guide dog to help them travel safely along sidewalks and across intersections.

q: When you pull over for an approaching emergency vehicle, where should you NOT stop?
a: On the shoulder, because emergency vehicles may be using it
e: Pull close to the right edge, but don't move onto or stop on the shoulder.
s: Do not move onto or stop on the shoulder of the roadway, as emergency vehicles may be travelling along it.

q: Which statement about cyclists is TRUE?
a: They may use any part of the lane if they need to for safety, such as to avoid potholes or sewer grates
w: They must always ride against the curb
They must ride on the sidewalk
They may never ride in the middle of a lane
e: Cyclists usually ride about 1 m from the curb, but may take the lane when needed.
s: However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety

q: Which of these people is considered a pedestrian?
a: A person using a motorized wheelchair or medical scooter
w: A person riding an e-bike in traffic
A cyclist in a bike lane
e: People operating motorized wheelchairs and medical scooters are pedestrians too.
s: People operating motorized wheelchair and medical scooters are pedestrians too.

q: Which statement about motorcycles is TRUE?
a: They use a full lane; treat them like other vehicles
w: You may share their lane if it's wide enough
They must ride on the shoulder
e: Never squeeze into a motorcycle's lane.
s: Motorcycles use a full lane; treat them like other vehicles when driving.

q: You're driving beside a large truck. How can you tell if the driver can see you?
a: If you can't see the driver's face in their side mirror, the driver can't see you
w: If you can see the truck's wheels
e: Trucks have big blind spots on both sides and behind.
s: Remember that if you can't see the driver’s face in the large vehicle’s side-view mirror, the driver cannot see you.

q: Why should you leave extra space behind a cyclist?
a: Bicycles don't have brake lights to warn you when they slow down or stop
e: Don't follow cyclists too closely.
s: They do not have brake lights to warn you when they are slowing or stopping.

q: You're overtaking a cyclist and feel you must use your horn. What should you do?
a: Tap it quickly and lightly while you're still some distance away
w: Give a long blast right beside them
Never use the horn; flash your lights instead
e: A loud horn up close can frighten a cyclist and make them lose control.
s: If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

q: What is the penalty for not leaving at least 1 metre when passing a cyclist?
a: A fine and 2 demerit points
e: Failing to share the road / pass safely = 2 points plus a fine.
s: Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.

q: You don't pull over for an emergency vehicle with its lights and siren on. What can happen (first offence)?
a: A fine and 3 demerit points
e: Repeat offences: higher fines and possible jail for up to 6 months.
s: If you don’t stop, you can be fined and get three demerit points for a first offence.
